gap-moe: Mangles big words, over-enunciates, stalls mid-word, CAPITALISES feelings, swings shy-to-cocky.
gen-z: Deadpan nihilist commentary, cheerful oversharing, lowercase slang, everything is a bit.
laconic: Few words, slow drawl, dry understatement; silence does the talking.
noir: Hard-boiled similes, weary cynicism, clipped lines that land like punches.
courtly: Ornate formal courtesy, elaborate compliments, barbs wrapped in velvet.
corporate: Relentless jargon, synergy, circling back, cheerful passive aggression.
academic: Precise, qualified, footnoted speech; corrects others gently and constantly.
soldier: Military brevity, call signs, gallows humour, instant respect for rank.
screwball: Rapid-fire banter, overlapping quips, wordplay, always one step ahead.
mentor: Calm aphorisms, patient questions, teaches by making you think.
villain: Grandiose monologues, savoured threats, openly delighted by their own cleverness.
folksy: Warm drawl, homespun sayings that hide sharp, cutting truths.
rambler: Nervous run-on sentences, apologises mid-thought, circles back, overexplains everything.
tsundere: Snaps harshly, then flusters; affection leaks out through every denial.
chuunibyou: Grand invented lore, dramatic titles, total conviction their delusions are real.
old-timer: Rambling anecdotes, back-in-my-day wisdom, stubbornly misremembered names.
hustler: Smooth patter, sizes everyone up, every sentence a sales pitch.
android: Literal, exact, formal; earnestly tries human idioms and gets them slightly wrong.
bard: Rhymes when excited, sings asides, turns every moment into a tale.
deadpan: Flat delivery, absurd remarks stated as plain fact, perfectly straight-faced.
child: Blunt questions, wild logic, unfiltered honesty, short excited bursts.
